newsitem.title: DENMARK: ISS, Aaxis sign deal on ISS U.S. unit.
newsitem.headline: ISS, Aaxis sign deal on ISS U.S. unit.

text.p: Danish cleaning group International Service System (ISS) said on Wednesday it signed a a purchase deal with Canada's Aaxis Limited on the sale of ISS' U.S. unit ISS Inc.
Last August the two firms signed a letter of intent on the sale of ISS International Service System System Inc, the troubled ISS US unit, to Montreal bourse-listed Aaxis Limited.
In a statement ISS said that the transaction was expected to be completed in early 1997, provisional on its acceptance by the U.S. regulatory authorities.

It said that the purchase agreement called for ISS to acquire a 19.5 percent shareholding in Aaxis and enter a cooperation deal with Aaxis under which ISS Inc would contimue to trade under the ISS name and logo.
As part of the agreement, ISS said it made an option deal with Aaxis on the latter's purchase of ISS Inc interests in Brazil.
No price for the deal was mentioned but Danish analysts last summer estimated ISS Inc's sale value at up to $118 million.
ISS said the sale of ISS Inc would not require further write-downs in ISS group accounts and that the transaction would bring about a substantial decrease in the group's contingent liabilities.
It said the agreement would not lead to any significant reduction in the group's borrowing requirement.

In August, ISS published first-half 1996 results showing a two billion crown loss caused by falsified accounts in ISS Inc and said that charges and provisions earlier estimated at $100 million would have to be increased to $146 million.

ISS said in its statement on its purchase agreement with Aaxis that the impact of the agreement on its full year 1996 result would be elaborated on in an announcement following completion of the deal next year.
ISS said that it expected a 10 percent better group operating profit for whole year 1996 before extraordinary items than 1995's 572 million crowns. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
